# Wisdom of Solomon Chapter 1 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Codex Vaticanus, Wisdom 1

---

**1:1** Love righteousness, you who are judges of the earth; think of the Lord in goodness, and seek him with sincerity of heart.

**1:2** For he is found by those who do not put him to the test, and he reveals himself to those who do not distrust him.

**1:3** For perverse thoughts separate one from God, and when his power is tested, it exposes the foolish.

**1:4** For wisdom will not enter a deceitful soul, nor will she dwell in a body enslaved to sin.

**1:5** For the holy spirit of discipline flees deceit, withdraws from thoughts without understanding, and is put to shame when unrighteousness draws near.

**1:6** For wisdom is a spirit that loves humanity, yet she will not acquit the blasphemer of his words; because God is witness of his inmost being, a true observer of his heart, and a hearer of his tongue.

**1:7** Because the spirit of the Lord has filled the inhabited world, and that which holds all things together has knowledge of every voice.

**1:8** Therefore no one who speaks unjust things will go unnoticed, and justice, when it brings judgment, will not pass him by.

**1:9** For inquiry will be made into the counsels of the ungodly, and a report of his words will come before the Lord as proof of his lawless deeds.

**1:10** Because an attentive ear hears all things, and the noise of complaints is not hidden.

**1:11** Therefore guard yourselves from worthless complaining, and keep your tongue from slander; for no secret word is without consequence, and a lying mouth destroys the soul.

**1:12** Do not seek death in the error of your life, nor bring destruction upon yourselves by the work of your hands.

**1:13** For God did not make death, and he takes no pleasure in the destruction of the living.

**1:14** For he created all things that they might have being; and the life-giving forces of the world are wholesome, and there is no destructive poison in them, nor is the dominion of Hades on earth.

**1:15** For righteousness is immortal.

**1:16** But it is the ungodly who by their hands and words have summoned death; counting it as a friend, they have wasted away, and they have made a covenant with it, because they deserve to belong to its company.

---

## Council Notes

**On 1:1 — "sincerity of heart":** SOPHIA adopts LOGOS's "sincerity of heart" over EMET's "simplicity" as it captures haplotēti's dual sense of integrity and undividedness. PNEUMA's "undivided heart" is vivid but paraphrastic.

**On 1:6 — "loves humanity":** SOPHIA retains EMET/LOGOS's "loves humanity" (philanthrōpon) over PNEUMA's "loves people" as the former preserves the Hellenistic philosophical register appropriate to this text.

**On 1:7 — "inhabited world":** SOPHIA adopts "inhabited world" (oikoumenē) from LOGOS over EMET's plain "world," restoring the Stoic cosmological resonance.

**On 1:14 — "life-giving forces":** SOPHIA synthesizes EMET's "generative forces" and PNEUMA's "life-giving forces" into "life-giving forces of the world" — preserving both the generative sense and the positive valence.

**On 1:15:** All agents agree this verse stands alone as a complete theological thesis: righteousness (dikaiosynē) is immortal (athanatos). No elaboration.

**Structural note:** The chapter moves through an argument: seek God (vv. 1–3) → sin blocks wisdom (vv. 4–6) → God hears all (vv. 7–10) → guard speech (v. 11) → do not seek death (vv. 12–14) → righteousness is immortal (v. 15) → the wicked chose death (v. 16). SOPHIA's rendering preserves this rhetorical arc.
